entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Agostino Casaroli was an Italian Catholic priest and diplomat for the Holy See, who became Cardinal Secretary of State in 1967. He played a crucial role in the Vatican's efforts to deal with the religious persecution of the Church in the nations of the Soviet bloc after the Second Vatican Council.

Born in Rome, Italy, around 1922, Casaroli entered the Jesuit order at a young age and was ordained as a priest in 1949. He served in various diplomatic posts, including in the Soviet Union and Poland, before becoming the Vatican's chief diplomat in 1967.

During his tenure, Casaroli oversaw the Vatican's negotiations with communist governments, including the Soviet Union, and played a key role in securing the release of Western hostages and negotiating the release of Polish prisoners.

Casaroli's legacy is marked by his commitment to interfaith dialogue and his efforts to promote peace and understanding between nations.

He died on June 9, 1998, in Rome, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most influential diplomats of the 20th century.
